title: Kimi read-only reviewer delegations get "user rejected the approval request" on authorized read-only tools (Engram reads, Bash date)
outcome: A Kimi review delegation started read-only can call the read-only tools its recovery needs, such as Engram read words (next --peek, memories, show) and harmless read-only shell commands, without an approval refusal. Writing tools and sandbox-escaping commands are still refused. If a read is refused, the child reports it as a host policy refusal, not as a user rejection.
acceptance: The refusal is reproduced or explained from source: which TermAl layer turns a Kimi read-only child's tool call into the ACP approval answer "the user rejected the approval request", and why it applies to authorized read-only calls (mcp__engram__next peek, Bash date) and not to the same calls in Codex or Claude read-only reviewer children.

In a Kimi read-only review delegation, the Engram read words needed for recovery and a read-only shell command run without an approval refusal, while a writing tool or write command is still refused; a test covers the generated Kimi delegation configuration or permission path for both cases.
A refused call in a Kimi child is labelled as a host policy refusal rather than a user rejection, so reviewers and parents do not report a user denial that never happened.
